problem:
Find, **in radians**, the **exact value** of the argument of $z=-5+5\sqrt{3}\text{i}.$

**Hint**: The argument of a complex number is in the range $[0,2\pi ).$ 

$arg⁡(z)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
Let's plot $z$ in the complex plane.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13930486/assets/f466a110eda3b07b50d988de6e46a541ad85d7ff64f43a6f056ea216752fa2d9.png)

The complex number $z$ lies in the second quadrant of the complex plane. Hence $\frac{\pi }{2}<arg⁡(z)<\pi .$ 

If $\alpha $ is the angle that $z$ makes with the negative real axis, then

$$
\begin{aligned}tan⁡\alpha  & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{5} \\ \alpha  & =arctan⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =arg⁡(z)=\pi -\frac{\pi }{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$
